messages.author: ba1d5380065b224f
messages.subject: Effective sample size in LDSC
parts:
Hi all,

How is the NEFF column used in the ldsc-function? Looking at the code and can't seem to find the place where it would be used for liability scale conversions. I assumed this would be with the new munge functionality for NEFF and NEFF_HALF etc, and from the wiki instructions to set the prevalences to a balanced sample in ldsc.

Kind regards,
Johan

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Effective sample size in LDSC
parts:
Hi Johan, 

NEFF is used just liked N; the munge output just lists it as N so if you are looking in the ldsc code itself for where that is being utilized that might be what is throwing you off. Since NEFF already has the liability correction applied at the level of sample size using N to back out SNP-based h^2 in the ldsc regression calculation functions the same as applying the liability correction after the fact. 

Best, 
  Andrew

messages.subject: Re: Effective sample size in LDSC
parts:
Thank you Andrew, I see it now. We are keeping a large repository of GWAS summary statistics where the munged versions are important not only for LDSC because they are standardised from the initial variety of data formats. Was thinking about whether any analysis (other than LDSC) would need the original N rather than NEFF, and then if there was any idea of making LDSC interpreting NEFF as N.

Best,
Johan
